name: Malar augmentation with fat grafting

lead: Malar fat grafting uses fat taken from elsewhere on the body, processed and injected into the cheeks to add fullness and projection.
It is discussed as a natural-tissue alternative to implants or fillers. Evidence specific to cheek augmentation is limited in the sources reviewed.

paras: Fat is harvested by liposuction, purified and reinjected into the cheek area; the portion that survives provides lasting volume, and the rest is resorbed.
Reported risks of fat grafting include swelling, bruising, infection, lumpiness or contour irregularity, fat necrosis and unpredictable resorption. It is a medical procedure performed by surgeons.

trials.title: Treatment of Atrophic Post Acne Scars by Fat Grafting

lead: Malar augmentation with fat grafting is a cosmetic procedure in which a person's own fat is harvested, usually by liposuction from another body site, processed, and injected into the cheek area to add volume and projection over the cheekbones.[1] It is a form of autologous (self-derived) soft-tissue augmentation, distinct from cheek implants and from hyaluronic acid fillers.

In appearance-focused communities it is discussed as a softer-tissue alternative to implants for fuller or more defined cheeks. General fat-grafting sources describe facial uses as restoring volume to deflated facial compartments, and note that some transferred fat is resorbed over time, so outcomes can vary.[1]

Published evidence specific to cheek augmentation is not included in the sources compiled here. The one registered trial linked to this entry studied fat grafting for acne scars, not cheek contour.[2]
infobox: Partial resorption, swelling, bruising, contour irregularity[1]

paras: Fat transfer is generally described as three stages: collecting fat, usually by liposuction; purifying it; and reinjecting it into the target area. It can be done under local or general anesthesia, and sources stress minimal handling and prompt reinjection to help the cells survive.[1]

Facial fat grafting is described as part of a shift from approaches that mainly removed skin and fat toward restoring volume lost in individual facial compartments with age.[1] Applied to the cheeks, the aim is greater fullness or projection in the malar region.

Complications listed for fat grafting in general include swelling, bruising, hematoma, donor-site pain or altered sensation, hypertrophic scarring, infection, contour irregularities, fat necrosis, and injury to underlying structures from the cannula.[1] Transferred fat is said to behave like fat elsewhere in the body, so large weight changes can alter results, and one general source notes that in breast augmentation the body may reabsorb up to half of the graft.[1] Figures for the cheek were not given.

No studies found on cheek (malar) augmentation specifically. A completed registered trial, NCT05028283 (n=69, started 2021), studied fat grafting for atrophic post-acne scars, a different indication.[2]

Fat grafting is generally discussed alongside implants, fillers and midface surgery as an option for cheek and midface volume. No forum thread was cited for this entry, so specific community claims are not documented here.
